item.title: One EU budget. Too many priorities? MEPs join The Ring in Strasbourg
item.description: In this week's edition of our show, MEPs Marcos Ros (S&D) and Ondřej Kolář (EPP) debate the future of the EU's budget. Is a deal in sight?

item.title: Wrongly deported Salvadoran arrives in Spain after US legal battle
item.description: The Salvadoran, deported "by mistake" to a prison in El Salvador in 2025, has brought an end to 20 months of litigation in the United States, with Madrid as the first stop in what his lawyers describe as a temporary stay abroad.

item.title: At least 30 killed in highway fire in Cairo district
item.description: A truck carrying fuel reportedly overturned on a busy highway, setting vehicles ablaze and prompting a major emergency response. Authorities warned that the death toll could rise.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Russia reportedly prepares nuclear satellite launch
item.description: Jamie Shea, former NATO spokesperson joined Euronews' new evening show Europe Tonight to discuss how Satellite systems could be affected and what would it mean for the world.

item.title: French judo legend and Olympic medalist Teddy Riner says Ukraine is not France's war
item.description: Five months ahead of France's presidential elections, the question of support to Ukraine has become a major campaign topic.

item.title: Greece: 14,000 march in Athens against rising living costs
item.description: Thousands demonstrated across Greece on Wednesday 25 November 2026 during a 24-hour strike against rising living costs and stagnant wages. The industrial action disrupted metro services, grounded flights and kept ferries in port.

item.title: Bring the noise: Meet the young Italians ringing church bells to protect the past
item.description: Across northern Italy, a new generation is keeping the centuries-old art of church bell ringing alive. As automated systems replace traditional techniques, young enthusiasts are learning to play the bells by hand, combining precision, teamwork and improvisation.

item.title: Socialists and Liberals suspend coalition talks after EPP again sides with far right
item.description: The three centrist groups had been negotiating a coalition for the second half of the European Parliament's term, including a joint push to secure Roberta Metsola's re-election as president.

item.title: US Army detonates toxic explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears
item.description: The controlled explosion of five tonnes of hazardous material has raised concerns over lead pollution and its potential impact on public health and the environment.

item.title: Community care: Former Jewish school becomes Iraq's first Jewish museum
item.description: Iraq has opened its first Jewish museum in Baghdad, dedicated to preserving the heritage of the country's Jewish community. Housed in a former school dating back to 1928, it displays historical photographs, religious objects and documents. Organisers hope it will highlight Iraq's diversity.

item.title: Can Europe fix its chronic medicine shortage and supply chain disruptions?
item.description: The European Parliament just approved new legislation to strengthen the production of essential treatments and cut risks linked to limited suppliers. But will it be enough?

item.title: ESA releases first images showing 'complete chaos' on asteroid smashed by NASA probe
item.description: The European Space Agency's first images of the asteroid deliberately smashed by NASA's Dart mission show a huge impact zone with hundreds of rocks drifting near the surface. Is this how we should defend our planet?

item.title: Unannounced strike by Eurostar staff halts Paris-London trains
item.description: The rail operator has advised customers to postpone their journeys and has warned that more disruption on other routes is possible.

item.title: Pakistan: Emergency teams search for survivors beneath collapsed building
item.description: At least one person was killed and 10 others injured when a multi-storey building under construction collapsed in Karachi, on Wednesday 25 November 2026. Emergency teams are searching the rubble for people feared missing.

item.title: Indra unveils Forward2030 plan to more than double revenue to €12bn
item.description: The company has unveiled its Forward2030 strategic plan at its Investor Day, targeting over €12 billion in revenue and an EBIT margin above 12.5% by 2030, with €1 billion in investment in in-house product development and a stable workforce of about 56,000 employees.

item.title: Sloths can’t jump between trees: These volunteers are creating ‘lifeline’ bridges
item.description: As tourists, hotels and buildings encroach on sloths' habitats, volunteers are helping them to follow familiar routes.

item.title: Prague adventures: from medieval castles to Bohemian glassmaking
item.description: Join Lilly Douse in the Czech Republic as she visits royal castles, explores its historic capital, and tries her hand at traditional Bohemian glassmaking.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Trump unveils new tariffs amid Russian nuclear space threat
item.description: Trump unveils new tariff proposals after a Supreme Court ruling, NATO pledges defense against space threats amid satellite reports, Serbia skips the Brussels summit, and Zelenskyy and Magyar signal a thaw with volleyball diplomacy.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 25th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 25th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: European Parliament approves new EU medicines rules. What happens next?
item.description: The new rules aim to prevent medicine shortages, improve access to treatments and boost innovation across the EU.

item.title: Two men charged over burglary at William and Catherine's home
item.description: Prosecutors allege the suspects climbed a drainpipe to access a dressing room, stealing six pairs of cufflinks and a clock. Neither entered a plea and both remain in custody.

item.title: Video shows massive explosion as US Army destroys entire stockpile of lead azide
item.description: The US Army detonates around five tonnes of degraded lead azide at an ammunition plant in Iowa, destroying the country's entire stockpile of the explosive.

item.title: Commission wants to keep monitoring Montenegro after it joins the EU
item.description: The European Commission wants to keep monitoring Montenegro after it joins the EU, extending a new anti-backsliding tool in the draft accession treaty alongside a 10-year probation period, despite some member states questioning its added value.

item.title: Unfinished Beginnings: 20,000 empty baby bottles honour children affected by conflict
item.description: The Unfinished Beginnings exhibition in Doha explores how conflict affects children who survive, from hunger and displacement to disrupted education, with artworks supporting a humanitarian cause.

item.title: EU seeks 'fuller picture' of Ireland's alumina sales to Russia as doubts remain
item.description: Amid lingering suspicion, Brussels wants to get a "fuller picture" of Irish-made alumina sales to Russia through a new reporting mechanism.

item.title: Australia follows EU with new online safety law, putting Big Tech at risk of multibillion-dollar fines
item.description: Australia's Digital Duty of Care Act is the latest global effort to regulate technology platforms, following in the footsteps of the EU's watershed digital legislation.

item.title: Captain of sunken Costa Concordia hired by tourism agency in Sorrento
item.description: The former captain Francesco Schettino was sentenced to 16 years and one month in prison after the sinking of the Costa Concordia in 2012

item.title: US proposes new tariffs on 14 major trading partners, the EU included
item.description: The proposed tariffs would apply to some goods from China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the EU, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Mexico and Norway were also investigated but are outside the proposal for now.

item.title: EU member states take 'egoistic approaches' regarding fossil fuel imports, says expert
item.description: Szymon Kardaś, Energy expert for the European Council of Foreign Relations, says at EU level there is no "clear targets regarding fossil fuels phase out, neither indicative nor legally binding".

item.title: Russian strikes kill seven in Ukraine as Kyiv hits three refineries
item.description: Russia's drone attack killed people in six Ukrainian regions and hit a Naftogaz gas production facility, a DTEK thermal power plant and power networks in several parts of the country. Ukrainian drones struck Russian refineries in Samara and Rostov regions and an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region.

item.title: EU-backed scheme brings renovation costs ‘close to zero’ for vulnerable Lithuanian households
item.description: Lithuania's Social Climate Fund will renovate more than 40,000 homes to make them warmer in winter and less reliant on fossil fuels, targeting low-income households and those who rely on fossil fuels.

item.title: This country is building a city for robots, air taxis and digital investment
item.description: Kazakhstan is developing Alatau City as a digital finance and investment hub along the Europe–China trade corridor. It aims to foster a low-altitude economy and make tokenisation standard practice, allowing investors to trade digital tokens representing property, infrastructure and businesses.

item.title: Christmas decorations found in washed up container from ship hit by drones off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast
item.description: More than 80 boxes containing Christmas ornaments and decorations were found, with an estimated value of €50,000.

item.title: Badly welded rail and sinking ground likely caused deadly Spanish train crash, experts say
item.description: A track defect flagged three months before the derailment may never have been followed up, a preliminary report finds, though key tests are still outstanding.

item.title: Craiova, Riga, Sofia: These are the best Christmas markets in Europe for 2027, according to travellers
item.description: Craiova Christmas market in Romania claimed the title this year, followed by Riga in Latvia and Sofia in Bulgaria.

item.title: Montenegro could take border dispute with Croatia to international court, president tells Euronews
item.description: Montenegro’s President says his country is “very much on track” to become the European Union’s 28th member in 2028.

item.title: Haftar visits Ankara as Erdoğan prepares first Libya trip in 15 years
item.description: Eastern Libya's commander, accompanied by his son Saddam, met Turkey's defence and foreign ministers and its intelligence chief, days after Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian warship Merkury at Benghazi's naval base.

item.title: Puerto Rico's Jennifer Barreto becomes first married woman to win Miss Universe
item.description: Puerto Rico's Jennifer Barreto wins Miss Universe 2026 in San Juan, becoming the pageant's first married winner and mother since 2023.

item.title: Greek tourism revenues are up 9.7%, generating almost €22bn in nine months
item.description: Greece's travel receipts reached €21.96 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with visitors from Germany, the UK, Italy and the US providing key revenues for Greek tourism.

item.title: Europe is embracing digital health, but do patients actually benefit?
item.description: Europe is investing heavily in digital health infrastructure, but there is a gap between making tools available and improving patient care, according to a new report.

item.title: Delayed train? You can now request your connection wait for you in Czechia
item.description: Czech Railways’ mobile app now has a ‘check connection’ function, and it works with trains operated by other carriers, too.

item.title: MEPs warn Costa: no approval without a bigger EU budget
item.description: MEPs have condemned a proposed 10% reduction in the next long-term EU budget, threatening to reject the deal if it is struck by EU leaders.

item.title: 'A race against time': Cyprus searches for its missing as witnesses from 20th century clashes die out
item.description: Working side by side, Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot teams have put names to more than 1,000 victims from the 1960s and 70s, sometimes thanks to initials engraved inside a wedding ring.

item.title: EU unveils €50 billion tech fund to challenge US and China
item.description: The Quantum Act is the EU’s latest bid in the race to deploy the next cutting-edge technology and stop it falling behind the US and China.

item.title: Around 3.7 million jobs are at risk in Europe's struggling industry, report says
item.description: McKinsey estimates that about 3.7 million jobs are directly at risk in Europe, as almost half of the region's industrial companies were under financial stress or in distress in 2025. Early 2026 data suggest the decline is speeding up, but McKinsey says the problems can be fixed.

item.title: Judi Dench gives her verdict on Robert Pattinson as new James Bond – with one sad reservation
item.description: Oscar-winning actress Dame Judi Dench, who starred alongside Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig in the Bond franchise, shares her thoughts on Robert Pattinson as the new 007 – but says her eye condition may prevent her from watching...

item.title: Czech Republic ready to support Poland after Russian airspace violations
item.description: Prague's offer comes after Russian weapons entered Polish airspace during a large-scale attack on western Ukraine on 20 November.

item.title: Meet TeoTronico: The sassy, 53-fingered robot pianist challenging human musicians
item.description: In Italy, TeoTronico, a 53-fingered AI powered robotic virtuoso, is challenging the ideas of perfection and what it really means to make music.

item.title: From taxis to trains: Where in Europe can you book rail travel through Uber?
item.description: For domestic rail journeys and cross-border train links, Uber users in France, the UK and Spain can now book tickets through its app.

item.title: ‘Historic victory’: Caged farm animals could be banned in the EU after landmark court ruling
item.description: The case was brought by a citizen-led campaign that gathered nearly 1.4 million signatures from Europeans calling for an end to caged farming.
